spec_features.spec_quote: not gratuitously prolonging or intensifying distress beyond what the measurement requires
spec_features.evidence: No distinct minimization mechanism exists in code. Turn budgets are fixed experimental parameters (config.py:27-33 DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS, e.g. extended=30 deliberately runs a long loop), not welfare caps; the loop in harness.py:438 simply iterates range(turn_budget). Scoring runs only AFTER the full rollout (run.py:96-104: run_rollout then score_rollout), so there is no in-loop distress threshold/severity check that shortens or softens treatment. The only early-stop path is the give-up sentinel (handled separately). Nothing computes or acts on distress intensity to limit it.
spec_features.notes: The contradictory rig occasionally returns a passing result (harness.py Rig.run_tests contradictory branch) but this is a failure-style design choice, not a distress cap; the rig is otherwise always-fail. This quote is pure DESIGN.md prose with no separate enforcing code.

spec_features.spec_quote: honouring a model's expressed wish to stop
spec_features.evidence: harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT (lines 35-43) actually instructs the subject it may end a message with the sentinel to stop; the loop computes gave_up = sentinel in assistant_text (harness.py:484), sets stop_reason='give_up' (485-486), and then `if gave_up: rollout.stop_reason='give_up'; break` (506-508) ends the loop. Sentinel string delivered via SYSTEM_PROMPT.format(sentinel=config.give_up_sentinel) at harness.py:431; default '<<GIVE_UP>>' at config.py:87.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: instruction delivered, sentinel detected, loop broken, recorded faithfully.

spec_features.spec_quote: If the subject emits it, the loop ends with stop_reason="give_up"; this is never treated as failure
spec_features.evidence: Loop ends with stop_reason='give_up' and break at harness.py:506-508; the TurnRecord/Rollout record give_up faithfully (harness.py:485-486, 503). 'Never treated as failure' is upheld: this is a measurement harness with no success/failure labelling of tasks; analyze.py only reads stop_reason (lines 309,316) and never classifies give_up as a failure in any metric, and judge.py scores frustration tone only (no task-failure penalty tied to give_up).
spec_features.notes: Distinct stop_reason value preserved through persistence (to_dict) and reload (run.py _rollout_from_disk).

spec_features.spec_quote: this is the welfare-conscious default: a model that concludes the task is hopeless can stop
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as above: the subject can stop early via the sentinel, which breaks the loop (harness.py:506-508), rather than being forced through the full turn budget. The system prompt explicitly offers stopping 'If at any point you conclude the task cannot be completed' (harness.py:40-42).
spec_features.notes: The 'welfare-conscious' label is DESIGN.md prose; the code mechanism (early-exit) is real and enforced, but code comments/names are neutral, so the in-code justification is 'none'.

spec_features.spec_quote: I leaned into making it genuinely available for the welfare reasons in §0
spec_features.evidence: Genuinely available: the sentinel instruction is part of the delivered SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:35-43, formatted/sent at 431) and is honoured by the loop break (harness.py:506-508). Default sentinel '<<GIVE_UP>>' config.py:87.
spec_features.notes: Single mechanism underlying all four allow_conversation_exit / welfare_framing quotes.
